comments.note: nodes/__init__.py line 445: ChunkWriter.__init__() (which calls mkdir) is NOT wrapped in a try/except. An OSError from disk-full or permission-denied would propagate out of the streaming try block and cause stage_success=False, failing an otherwise healthy agent run. The slug_dir derivation (lines 417-433) is guarded, but ChunkWriter instantiation is not. Recommend wrapping lines 444-448 in a try/except OSError to degrade gracefully (set _slug_dir=None, log at WARNING, continue without chunk capture).

AIMessageChunk items with id=None are silently dropped from _msgs reconstruction. In nodes/__init__.py: None-id chunks are stored in _chunk_accumulator[None] (overwriting each other) and added to _msg_order as ('chunk', None); the reconstruction guard 'if _mid is not None' then drops them. Modern LangGraph always assigns IDs so in practice this is benign, but it is an untested failure mode. If a provider ever emits un-ID'd chunks, final_content would be unexpectedly empty.

summary: Code review FAIL — two blocking issues found. (1) ChunkWriter.__init__() instantiation is unguarded: an OSError from mkdir/open propagates into the outer streaming try-block and causes stage_success=False for an otherwise-healthy agent run. The slug_dir derivation block immediately above it (lines 416-433) is correctly guarded with try/except, but the instantiation itself (lines 444-447) is not. Fix: wrap ChunkWriter(...) in try/except OSError; on failure set _slug_dir=None, log at WARNING, and continue without chunk capture — matching the existing slug_dir guard pattern. (2) _slug_dir / slug derivation logic is duplicated verbatim at three independent sites: (a) the ChunkWriter pre-stream setup block (lines 417-433), (b) the post-stream Markdown dialogue capture block (lines 545-553), and (c) the error-path Markdown capture block in the except handler (lines 732-740). If the storage path ever changes, all three sites must be updated in sync — a latent DRY violation on a critical path. Fix: extract a private _derive_slug_dir(state, workspace_root) helper returning Path|None and call it once before the streaming block; pass the result through. All other aspects of the implementation are clean: ChunkWriter try/finally is correct, AIMessageChunk accumulation logic is sound, dialogue backward-compatibility preserved, tests comprehensive.

comments.note: BLOCKING — nodes/__init__.py lines 443-448: ChunkWriter instantiation is unguarded. After the guarded _slug_dir derivation block (lines 416-433), the code does `_chunk_writer = ChunkWriter(slug_dir=_slug_dir, ...)` without any try/except. ChunkWriter.__init__() calls chunks_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and then dest.open('w') — either call can raise OSError (disk-full, permission-denied, read-only filesystem). That OSError propagates up into the outer streaming try-block and is caught by the broad `except Exception` on line 655, resulting in stage_success=False and a stage_error log for what is fundamentally a non-critical capture feature. The fix is a small try/except OSError wrap exactly matching the pattern used for slug_dir derivation above: try: _chunk_writer = ChunkWriter(slug_dir=_slug_dir, wp_id=_wp_id, stage=stage); _chunk_file_path = _chunk_writer.path; except OSError: log.warning('Could not open chunk file for %s/%s; chunk capture disabled for this run.', _wp_id, stage); _slug_dir = None. This ensures capture failures never cause agent stage failures.

BLOCKING — nodes/__init__.py: _slug_dir / slug derivation logic is duplicated at three sites: (a) lines 417-433 (pre-stream ChunkWriter setup), (b) lines 545-553 (post-stream Markdown dialogue capture), (c) lines 732-740 (error-path Markdown dialogue capture). All three compute exactly the same value: Path(state['project_path']).name → slug, workspace_root / 'mcp-server' / 'storage' / 'ledger' / slug → slug_dir. This is a DRY violation on a hot path: any future change to the storage structure (e.g. renaming 'mcp-server' or the 'ledger' subdirectory) requires three independent edits with no compiler safety net. Fix: extract a private module-level helper `def _derive_slug_dir(project_path: str, workspace_root: Path) -> Path | None` that encapsulates the derivation (including the try/except for the state key access). Call it once near the top of node_fn() before the streaming block, store the result in a local variable, and pass it through to all three use sites. The slug_dir needed for the error-path capture is already declared before `try` so this is a straightforward refactor with no behavioral change.

Non-blocking observation (surfaced by Developer, confirmed here): nodes/__init__.py lines 462-479: the double-TypeError fallback for non-serialisable chunk metadata silently swallows failures after the second retry (bare `pass`). A one-line log.debug call on the second except would make it trivially diagnosable when chunk data is silently dropped. Not blocking — current behavior is correct, just opaque.

Non-blocking: the `_msg_order` list stores `('chunk', _msg_id)` tuples where `_msg_id` may be None. The reconstruction loop at lines 503-509 then guards `if _mid is not None`. This works, but the convention of storing None as a key in both the accumulator dict and the order list is mildly surprising. A future cleanup could skip None-id chunks entirely at accumulation time (lines 484-490) and add a log.debug warning to surface the unexpected case. Not blocking for this WP since modern LangGraph always assigns IDs.
